name: Install DevStack
description:
we covered these steps on OpenStack basics under topic Install and Configure DevStack. And couple of time during Cinder and Glance. This time, we will run a wrapper script which will download the repo and setup config files. Just run the wrapper script after updating the system 
sudo apt-get update  
sudo apt-get -y install git

wget -O- http://giis.co.in/install_devstack.sh | bash

Okay done, please check the local.conf and openrc files. Lets run the devstack script, you know it will around ~30 minutes.

sudo su stack
cd ~
 /home/stack/openstack/stack.sh

name: OpenStack Commandline
description:
So far, we have used Horizon dashboard to create instance, but real admins use command-line :) On this lesson we will use commandline to practise and learn about following tasks:


  • Creating an instance
  • Creating key-pair
  • Logging into instance
  • Pause and unpause an instance
  • Suspend and resume an instance
  • Shelve and unshelve an instance
  • Soft and hard reboot an instance
  • Delete instance

We have exported env variable like OS_AUTH_URL,OS_USERNAME,OS_PASSWORD, OS_TENANT_NAME,OS_PROJECT_NAME on /home/stack/openstack/openrc file we need to import them into our current shell like
source openrc
Note: OS_PROJECT_NAME and OS_TENANT_NAME are same except OS_PROJECT_NAME preferred in recent times. OS_TENANT_NAME is for back compatibility.

name: Launch instances
description:
We need use
nova boot
to boot an instance. But wait! we need to pass few more parameters to it,will see them below. To launch an instance we need to available flavors (types). List the available flavors (instance types) and note the ID of the flavor that you want to use for your instance.
nova flavor-list
We will use ID=1
nova boot --flavor 1
Now we need image, to list the available images:
nova image-list
We will use first cirros.
nova boot --flavor 1 --image cirros-0.3.4-x86_64-uec
We need to set security group (which tells what ports to open etc). to list them
nova secgroup-list

nova boot --flavor 1 --image cirros-0.3.4-x86_64-uec --security-groups default
Every looks fine, we have instance type and image and secuirty group, but one thing is missing, after the instance booted how we going to ssh into it? We need a keypair for it. So lets create it. Its our final step.
nova keypair-add cloudkey > cloudkey.pem

chmod 600 cloudkey.pem
We can list the key pairs via
nova keypair-list
We will set the instance name as wmvm and launch it like:
nova boot --flavor 1 --image cirros-0.3.4-x86_64-uec --security-groups default --key-name cloudkey wmvm
We can check the status with command
nova list
will list ID,Name along with 
 State: Active  | Power state: Running | Networks:private=10.0.0.2
show information about your server, including its size, which is shown as the value of the flavor property.
nova show wmvm

name: Logging into an Instance
description:
We just launched an instance, can we verifing this with Horizon Dashboard?. Answer is 'Yes', afterall, whenever we use Horizon dashboard, they invoke these commands internally. So login to dashboard with admin/password and see for yourself. Needless to say, Dashboard URL:

 http://HOST_IP

In fact, whatever you do on commandline should reflect on Horizon dashboard. If it didn't, congrats you found a bug in OpenStack Horizon :) Please file a bug on OpenStack or write to us we will file it on your behalf!
Lets login
ssh -i cloudkey.pem cirros@10.0.0.2

Play around with this instance and type
exit
to logout from this instance.

name: Pause and unpause an instance
description:
Pause command stores the state of the VM in RAM. A paused instance continues to run in a frozen state To pause an instance, run the following command
nova pause wmvm

nova unpause wmvm

name: Suspend and Resume
description:
To initiate a hypervisor-level suspend operation, run the following command:
nova suspend wmvm
To resume a suspended instance,
nova resume wmvm

name: Shelve and Unshelve Instance
description:
Shelving is useful if you have an instance that you are not using, but would like retain in your list of servers. For example, you can stop an instance at the end of a work week, and resume work again at the start of the next week. All associated data and resources are kept; however, anything still in memory is not retained. If a shelved instance is no longer needed, it can also be entirely removed. Shelving stops the instance and takes a snapshot of it. Then depending on the value of the shelved_offload_time config option, the instance is deleted from the hypervisor (0), never deleted (-1), or deleted after some period of time (> 0).
nova shelve wmvm
Unshelve an instance - Restores the instance.
nova unshelve wmvm

name: Reboot and Delete an instance
description:
You can soft or hard reboot a running instance. A soft reboot attempts a graceful shut down and restart of the instance. A hard reboot power cycles the instance.
nova reboot wmvm

nova reboot --hard wmvm
To completely delete an instance type
nova delete wmvm

So that marks the end of our nova related commandline. Hope you learned few things :) see you later
Source : http://docs.openstack.org/
